_comment: Step 0 of Phase 3. The complete current -> Figma -> new mapping for every semantic CSS token. NOTHING is migrated until this is approved: the rename cannot be re-derived halfway through. Drives scripts/ the migration once signed off.
_vocabulary: New CSS names follow Figma's Mapped groups: surface-*, text-*, border-*, status-*, plus brand-* which Figma lacks and gains. Utility names follow: --surface-card -> bg-surface-card.
_rule: Tokens that share a value are NOT collapsed. --ring equals --primary today, but focus and brand are different roles and Figma already separates them (Border/focus vs Status/info). Same value, different name, deliberately.

--foreground.status: exists; Figma repointed to this value

--destructive-foreground.status: ADD to Figma. NOT a duplicate of --text-inverse: it stays #f4faff in dark where --primary-foreground flips to #061b2e. Light text on a red fill, in both themes.

--border.status: exists; Figma repointed to this value

--switch-background.status: ADD to Figma. NOT a duplicate of --border: dark is #1971bf against the border's #145b99.

brand._note: Figma's Mapped has no brand group. Status/info aliases Primary/Base, but that is a usage, not the brand itself. Button/primary-bg resolves to Light Mode/1000 (#2a2e32, near-black), which contradicts P-CO1 — corrected to Primary/Base. A Color/Brand/* group is added to Figma.

--ember-hover.status: ADD; light value becomes Blue/600 #1971bf per ruling

invariant._note: Theme-invariant primitives used directly, not semantic roles. --chalk is named in Law L-C6 ("text on primary is always text-chalk") and used 426 times, so renaming it means amending a Law. FLAGGED FOR DECISION — see _openDecisions.

sidebarFamily._note: No Figma equivalent. Several are duplicates of the general tokens and retire; the rest are added to Figma as Color/Sidebar/*.

--sidebar-accent.status: ADD to Figma; light adopts Figma #e8f3fc

_summary.note: 14 of 38 semantic tokens are exact duplicates of another token in BOTH themes. Retiring them is the single biggest simplification here — it removes over a third of the semantic surface before a single usage is renamed.
_summary.verified: Every duplicate claim was checked against both themes, not assumed. Two failed that check and are kept distinct: --destructive-foreground (theme-invariant, unlike --primary-foreground) and --switch-background (dark #1971bf, not the border's #145b99).

_openDecisions: --chalk (426 uses) is named explicitly in Law L-C6. Renaming it to --text-on-brand means amending that Law. Keep --chalk as an exception to the Figma vocabulary, or rename and amend L-C6?
--midnight (35 uses) is the same question at much smaller scale.
16 duplicate tokens are marked retire. Confirm none of them are meant to diverge later — e.g. --popover is identical to --card today, but a future elevated surface might want its own value.
